sections.text: Introduction

This document details the items which are checking. They include testing
and the inspections, in addition to the procedures listed it expected the
checks which are done frequently, would also be completed at this time.

The first draft is initiated by eng. Ekramy Mostafa Mohamad. Accepted by
technical expert eng. Hassan Elbehiry
and Quality
Control general director eng. Gamal Abd Elwahab, and approved by eng.
Mohamad Gamal Diab Head sector of Inspection and quality control sector.
Safety Precautions

Disconnect
all power to motor prior to initiating any maintenance or repairs.

Avoid
contact with rotating parts.

Act
with care in accordance with prescribed procedures, in handling and lifting
this equipment.

Be
sure unit is electrically grounded and proper electrical installation wiring
and controls are used consistent with local and national electrical codes. refer to "national electrical code handbook" 
NFPA NO. 70. employ qualified electricians.

Be
sure equipment is properly enclosed to prevent access by children or other
unauthorized personnel in order to pre vent possible accidents.

Be
sure shaft key is fully captive before unit is energized.

Always
be sure oil lubricated units are filled with correct oil to proper level before
operating.

Provide proper safeguards for personnel
against rotating parts and applications involving high inertia loads which can
cause overspeed.

Avoid extended exposure to equipment with high
noise levels.

Observe good safety habits at all times and
use care to avoid injury to yourself or damage to your equipment.

Be familiar with the equipment and read
all instructions thoroughly before installing or working on equipment.

sections.text: Start-up Preparations after Storage

Motor should be thoroughly inspected
and cleaned to restore to an "As Shipped" condition.

Motors which have been subjected to
vibration must be disassembled and each bearing inspected for damage.

Oil and/or grease must be completely
changed using lubricants recommended on the motor's lubrication plate, or in
the Installation and Instruction Manual. After changing grease, the motor
should be run under no load with the drain plug removed. This will allow all
excess grease to be purged from the bearing cavity without danger to the
winding. After running, replace drain plug.

The winding must be tested to obtain
insulation resistance and dielectric absorption ratio as described in Section
III, Part 3.

If storage has exceeded one year, the U.S.E.M.
Quality Assurance Department, must be contacted prior to equipment start-up.

sections.text:
Final 
Alignment

items:
Check to assure that
 coupling hubs are not eccentric. Mount a dial indicator on a stationary part
 and read the eccentricity of the outside diameters of the coupling hubs as
 they are rotated.

Check to be sure
 that the motor feet lie in the same plane. Bolt the feet down securely. Mount
 a dial indicator on the driven half of the coupling. Take readings of the
 movement of the motor half of the coupling as the feet bolts are loosened.
 loosen a shaft end foot bolt, take a reading and
 re-tighten. On the same side of the motor, loosen the opposite shaft-end
 foot bolt and take a reading. Now add shims to the feet until motion of
 the coupling is less than 0.003" when either foot bolt is loosened.
 Repeat this procedure for the foot bolts on the opposite side of the
 motor.

Check for angular misalignment
 of motor to driven unit shaft. (See Figure 3A.) Measure distance between
 coupling hub faces (with feeler gauges) at four places equally spaced
 around the outside diameters. Position motor as necessary to be within the
 max allowable
 misalignment of 0.001 in. per foot of coupling radius.

Check for offset
 alignment. Fasten a dial indicator on one coupling hub with the indicator
 button contracting the alignment surface of the opposite coupling hub.
 (See figure 3B) rotate shaft onto which the indicator is attached and take
 readings at four points 90 Deg. apart. Relocate motor until total
 indicator movement, in a full rotation does not exceed .002 inches.
 Transfer indicator to opposite hub and repeat the offset alignment
 procedure. Recheck angular alignment as described in Step C.

Miscellaneous
 After each corrective adjustment, tighten the foot bolts securely and
 recheck alignment. When making shim adjustments, change only one foot at a
 time. Recheck alignment after the motor has been in service approximately
 one week. Readjust as necessary.

Part
winding starters used with part winding start motors should have the timer set
at a minimum time consistent with the power company requirements.

Two
seconds is the recommended maximum time on part winding.

Setting
the timer for longer periods can cause permanent damage to the motor, and may void
the warranty.

restarting of the motor before attempting to change any electrical connections.

After alignment has
been completed. run motor at minimum possible load (uncoupled from driven
equipment if possible) and check for vibration. If vibration is excessive (See
Table 1) loosen one Motor Mounting. Bolt.

If. vibration decreases add shims and retighten bolt. Repeat as
necessary for all bolts until vibration is reduced to acceptable limits.
Recheck. coupling alignment after any change in shims.

Recheck vibration after unit has
run under full load and has reached operating temperature.

sections.text: Reassembly

items:
Clean all
 machined and mating surfaces on bearing caps, bracket fits. etc.

Remove old
 grease from grease cavities and refill cavities approximately 50% full
 with recommended grease. See Table 2 for correct grease.

Carefully inspect
 ball or roller bearings for nicks, dents or any unusual wear patterns.
 Replace bearing if damaged.

Reassemble motor
 by reversing the disassembly procedure in Section VIII
 "Disassembly", Part 2, Items A through
 F. Bearings should be installed per bearing manufacturers recommended
 procedure.

Touch up any
 scratched or chipped paint to protect motor surfaces.

LUBRICATION

Motor must be at rest
and electrical controls should be locked open to prevent energizing while being
serviced. If motor is being taken out of storage refer to Section III
"Storage", Part 9 for preparation instructions.
Lubrication of Ball and Roller Bearing Motors
General

Units with grease lubricated bearings are pre-lubricated
at the factory and normally do not require initial lubrication. Refer to Table2
for recommended greases and suggested. re-greasing
intervals for longest bearing life.

Motors with Automatic
Grease. Drain Construction (See Figure 4A)

To re-lubricate bearings, add new grease until
clean grease flows from the drain (drain is behind the grill and is
automatically activated by the re-greasing operation).
Grease accumulations at drain should be removed to prevent grease entering the
motor. Excess

grease
in bracket reservoir will be automatically purged while motor is running.

The lower grill should be
removed periodically and any hardened or excess grease

manually
cleaned from bracket reservoir, drain and grill.

Lubrication of Ball and Roller Bearing Motors
General
Units with grease lubricated bearings are pre-lubricated
at the factory and normally do not require initial lubrication. Refer to Table2
for recommended greases and suggested. re-greasing
intervals for longest bearing life.
Motors with Automatic
Grease. Drain Construction (See Figure 4A)
To re-lubricate bearings, add new grease until
clean grease flows from the drain (drain is behind the grill and is
automatically activated by the re-greasing operation).
Grease accumulations at drain should be removed to prevent grease entering the
motor. Excess
grease
in bracket reservoir will be automatically purged while motor is running.
The lower grill should be
removed periodically and any hardened or excess grease
manually
cleaned from bracket reservoir, drain and grill.
